behavioral_effects: docker job: matrix over backend, frontend, docling-mcp, chrome-devtools-mcp on every push and PR, per-image GHA cache scope, Trivy table plus JSON artifact (90 days), PR short-circuit via dorny/paths-filter
publish job: after ci-ok on main and v* tags, docker/metadata-action tags, GHCR login with GITHUB_TOKEN, build-push from the warmed cache
trivy-image-scan statement and trivy-advisory-deliberate scope now name all four images; ci-ok needs docker
compatibility_impact: The docker job now runs on every event as a four-image matrix (PR builds skip an image whose context is untouched) and ci-ok depends on it. Images publish to ghcr.io/flux29/fullstack-{backend,frontend,docling-mcp,chrome-devtools-mcp} tagged sha-<short> and main on main pushes, X.Y.Z and latest on v* tags. The frontend image bakes NEXT_PUBLIC_* from repository variables with localhost defaults, so it is validation-only until those variables are set. Nothing pulls these images yet: make prod still builds locally.
follow_up: After the first main push: confirm ghcr.io/flux29/fullstack-backend:sha-<short> pulls from the dev machine and set package visibility deliberately
Phase 5a: LLM_PROVIDER=test fake provider so the e2e chat specs run without a live model
limitations: Simplification pass: not run; the change is workflow YAML and two governance data edits
Phase 4 of the CI/CD coverage plan. Not here: a compose override that pulls ghcr images (which would turn make prod into a pull-based deploy), e2e, nightly, Trivy promotion
reason: Only the backend image was ever built in CI, only on pushes to main, so a broken frontend or MCP sidecar Dockerfile reached main unnoticed and Trivy never saw three of the four images; the pipeline also delivered nothing - the one image it built was discarded. After this change every push and PR builds all four images with per-image layer caches and Trivy reports on each (still advisory, now with JSON evidence for the promotion ladder), and pushes to main and v* tags publish them to ghcr.io/flux29 as the first delivery step.
risks: GHCR package visibility defaults to private on first push and inherits nothing from the repository; the packages page must be checked after the first publish
PR short-circuit means a Dockerfile change reaching main through a PR that did not touch its context is only built on the main push - acceptable because ci-ok on main is the fix-forward signal
rollback: git revert stops the publish; images already pushed to GHCR remain and are deleted by hand from the packages page if unwanted.
security_impact: The publish job is the first job with packages: write, scoped to that job only, gated on ci-ok, and limited by if to pushes on main and v* tags; it logs in with the ephemeral GITHUB_TOKEN. The docker job gains pull-requests: read for paths-filter. Trivy now covers all four images (advisory, unchanged exit-code 0) and stores JSON reports for 90 days as the promotion-ladder evidence. Published images are pulled by digest-pinned bases and built from GHA layer caches scoped per image; zizmor's cache-poisoning concern is recorded in .github/zizmor.yml.
summary: Build and scan all four container images on every CI event and publish them to GHCR from main and release tags
